evidence: All survivors check `p1 + p2 > T` and then compare `sum1`/`sum2` against `T`; for example, `if p1 + p2 > T: print(f"JOB {i}")` and `if sum1 > T: print("LOAD 1")`.
affordance_in_statement: Individual Feasibility: A single item i cannot complete its sequential progression through both phases within the time allowed by the deadline T. Phase Saturation: The total duration of active work assigned to a single phase c across all j items cannot fit within the time allowed by the deadline T.
removal_suggestion: This cannot be removed by wording alone without changing the task: the certificate categories and the serial two-phase structure make these lower bounds intrinsically sufficient under the stated guarantee. A harder variant must permit schedule-level impossibility causes or require an actual schedule rather than only JOB/LOAD certificates.

common_affordance: The certificate is completely determined by intrinsic necessary lower bounds: p1+p2>T certifies JOB i, while sum(p1)>T or sum(p2)>T certifies LOAD 1 or LOAD 2.
recommended_edit: Replace the promised two-category impossibility guarantee with a schedule-level task whose valid certificate can depend on interactions between jobs and phases, or require constructing/verifying a schedule; merely rewording the current guarantee will not defeat these solutions.
